To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a coarse‐grain hybrid molecular dynamics approach was proposed and tested for simulating the electrophoretic separation of macromolecules in explicit solvent of a large number of solvent molecules.

a coarse‐graining approach was developed to simulate the electrophoresis dynamics of DNA in a system with explicit solvent particles, which was validated by the simulation of a simple polymer solution and the computation of the nonuniform charge distribution of a cylindrical nanotubes.

the CGH‐MD approach can be applied to the simulation DNA electrophores in explicit solvent of a large number of solvent molecules and the simulation results are consistent with those from more rigorous computational methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a coarse‐graining hybrid‐molecular dynamics approach for simulating DNA‐based microfluidic systems.
developing a new coarse‐grained molecular dynamics method for simulating electrophoresis processes in systems with large number of solvent molecules.
the development of a coarse‐grain hybrid molecular dynamics approach for the simulation of DNA and protein electrophoresis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of this study are not conclusive.
the results obtained by the coarse-grained hybrid molecular dynamics method are in excellent agreement with the results obtained by explicit solvent molecular dynamics method, but at much lower cost.
CGH‐MDS is a promising approach for simulating DNA and other macromolecules electrophoresis, especially in nanoscale systems that involve large numbers of solvent particles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a hybrid molecular dynamics approach that combines the advantages of explicit solvent models and coarse‐grained models.
the coarse-grained hybrid molecular dynamics is a promising method for studying DNA electrophoreses in explicit solvent systems with large number of solvent molecules.

a coarse‐grain hybrid molecular dynamics (cg‐hmd) method was developed to study the electrophoresis behaviors of DNA and other macromolecules in explicit solvent of extremely large number of particles, and the cg‐hmd approach was successfully applied to study the electroporetic behaviors of DNA in nanofludic, microfluidic and microstructure array devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hybrid molecular dynamics method can be applied to the simulation and design of DNA electrophoretic devices.

the CGH‐MD approach is useful for simulating electrophoresis processes of macromolecules in nanofludic, microfluidic and microstructure array devices that involve extremely large numbers of solvent particles.
we have developed a new coarse‐grained model for DNA electrophoreses that is computationally fast and accurate enough to be useful for the design of microfluidic devices.
